title: Spider
summary: Two-deck patience with 1, 2 or 4 suits, winnable deals and honest hints
description:
**Spider** is the two-deck patience game: ten columns, a stock of five deals, and eight runs from king to ace to put away. Play with one suit, two suits or four. No ads between games, no account, no tracking.

**Know where you stand**

- A calm light beside the move count stays green while a way to win is known. It turns amber once the game can no longer be won, and one tap takes you back to the last position that can still be won.
- Spider has so many ways to play that the solver cannot always be sure in the time it has. Then the light shows a hollow ring and says "not sure": it never guesses, and "can no longer be won" only shows when it is certain.
- Honest hints: Hint shows the next move of a real way to win, found by a solver that knows the face-down cards. When it finds none in time, it says so and offers to keep looking, instead of pointing at any move that happens to fit.
- The solver works beside the game, so the cards never wait for it, and it needs no internet.

**Deals**

- One suit for a gentle game, two suits, or four suits for the hardest.
- Winnable deals by default: every one of them has been won by the solver, 300 with one suit, 250 with two and 150 with four. Or play any deal at all.
- A daily deal for the suits you play, with a calendar of the days you solved. Missed days can still be played, and nothing nags you about streaks.

**Easy to play**

- Tap a card to pick it up with the cards on it, then tap the column where it should go. Cards of one suit in order move together; when cards cannot move together, the game says why.
- Tap the stock to deal a row. The stock shows how many deals are left, and the game tells you when an empty column must be filled first.
- A finished run from king to ace goes away by itself. Undo as many moves as you like. Once nothing is hidden and a way to win is known, the rest plays out by itself; that can be switched off. One-tap moves, dragging and the keyboard work too.

**Cards you can read**

- Three card sizes. Until you choose, the game picks the size that matches your phone's text size, and your choice stays. Ten columns are a tight fit on a phone, so turn it sideways for the biggest cards: the stock and the finished runs move to the sides.
- Bold, drawn ranks and suits that a large text setting never cuts off, and a high-contrast switch. Four suit colours are on from the start, so clubs and spades, hearts and diamonds never look alike.
- The stock on the left or on the right. Two card styles, six card shapes, eight card backs and six tables, all open from the start.

**Your game and your numbers**

- The game in progress, your settings and your statistics are saved after every move, Undo included, so you can close the app and carry on later. Inside the app they are part of the app's own data.
- Statistics for one, two and four suits: games played and won, win rate, best time, fewest moves, and your current and longest winning streak.

**Easy to use**

- Light and dark, English or Slovak, and screen-reader labels for every card, column and the stock. The win celebration is short and stays still when your phone asks for reduced motion.

**What it never does**

- No ads, no in-app purchases, no coins and no hints to buy.
- No account and no sign-in.
- No internet access: the game works offline and cannot connect anywhere.
- No analytics or tracking of any kind.

research.used_for: The rules (two decks, ten columns of six and five cards, a stock of five deals, runs of one suit moving together, no deal while a column is empty, eight runs from king to ace to win) and the one-, two- and four-suit levels
Read through a search summary: features expected of the type, such as one, two or four suits, unlimited undo, hints, daily challenges and statistics
Read through a search summary: one suit with spades only and two suits with spades and hearts, and missed daily challenges that can still be played
